summary: Recent relevant submissions emphasize geometry-response limits in relativistic heavy-ion inference, femtoscopic sensitivity to the dense-matter equation of state, small-x saturation observables in UPC/diffractive heavy-quark production, and practical AI/ML workflows for nuclear DFT, dipole-evolution surrogates, HEP anomaly detection, and scientific data compression.
strongest_paper_summary: arXiv:2609.01229 gives the most directly useful heavy-ion contribution: it quantifies parameter degeneracies that limit extraction of nuclear surface diffuseness from geometry-driven observables.

papers.title: Fundamental geometric limitations on disentangling nuclear-surface properties in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.authors_short: Hadi Mehrabpour, Behnaz Behzadmoghaddam, S. M. A. Tabatabaee Mehr, Oscar Garcia-Montero, Li Yan
papers.abstract: The extraction of the nuclear surface diffuseness from relativistic heavy ion collisions is limited by the intertwined responses of geometry-driven observables to surface diffuseness and intrinsic nuclear deformation. The authors use event-by-event Monte Carlo Glauber simulations, multidimensional response maps, information-geometric measures, and Bayesian analysis to identify local degeneracies among surface diffuseness and quadrupole/octupole deformation parameters.

papers.title: Femtoscopy as a New Probe of the Nuclear Equation of State
papers.authors_short: Xialei Jiang, Jiaxing Zhao, Yingjie Zhou, Xiaofeng Luo
papers.abstract: Using PHQMD transport calculations for Au+Au at sqrt(sNN)=3, 4.5, 7.7, and 19.6 GeV, the paper argues that nuclear mean fields add a dynamical low-k* contribution to two- and three-body femtoscopic correlations, with sensitivity to equation-of-state stiffness and momentum dependence.

papers.title: Saturation effects in diffractive deep inelastic scattering
papers.authors_short: Jani Penttala, Christophe Royon, Jarno Vierros
papers.abstract: The paper compares inclusive and diffractive heavy-quark photoproduction predictions with nonlinear BK and linear BFKL dipole evolution, focusing on UPC-accessible kinematics. It predicts roughly doubled coherent diffractive fractions in the saturation model relative to PDF/shadowing baselines.

papers.title: Neural-Network-Based Variational Method in Nuclear Density Functional Theory: Application to the Kohn-Sham method
papers.abstract: The authors represent complex spinor single-particle orbitals with multilayer perceptrons in a Kohn-Sham nuclear DFT setting, analyze tangent-space equivalence to the variational condition, and compare binding energies, charge radii, deformations, and nuclear pasta configurations against conventional calculations and experiment where applicable.

papers.title: Probing Dense Nuclear Matter at Small-x: A workflow for a global analysis framework
papers.authors_short: Junaid S. Khan, Rebecca L. Lustberg, Fredrick Olness, Peter Risse, Bjoern Schenke, Brandon Stevenson
papers.abstract: This proceedings contribution proposes ML surrogates for nonlinear dipole-nucleus evolution to reduce the computational cost of global analyses while retaining accuracy on relevant experimental-data descriptions.

papers.title: Anomaly detection for multijet scenarios
papers.authors_short: Gregor Kasieczka, Sung Hak Lim, Louis Moureaux, Tore von Schwartz, David Shih, Chitrakshee Yede
papers.abstract: The paper extends weakly supervised HEP anomaly detection beyond dijet-resonance assumptions by combining recursive soft drop with CATHODE for arbitrary multijet final states.

papers.title: Multivariate Scientific Data Compression with Learned Cross-Variable Latent Decorrelation and Autoregressive Entropy Modeling
papers.authors_short: Liangji Zhu, Anand Rangarajan, Sanjay Ranka
papers.abstract: CAESAR-LDAR is an error-controlled learned compressor for multivariate scientific fields, combining a trainable orthogonal latent transform with a causal autoregressive hierarchical prior and residual correction to meet reconstruction tolerance.

papers.title: Learning PDE Time-Stepping with Neural Cellular Automata
papers.abstract: A neural cellular automata surrogate learns local homogeneous update rules for PDE time stepping and is benchmarked against PDE-Net, a modified PINN, and FNO on canonical PDEs, including extrapolation beyond the training time horizon.

cautions.title: Reining in an Agentic Harness for High Energy Physics
cautions.reason: Useful community-design discussion, but the abstract signals principles and proposed contracts rather than a validated HEP agent benchmark. Treat as workflow architecture, not demonstrated scientific capability.

cautions.title: Spin alignment of vector mesons in a plasma at finite density
cautions.reason: The observable is relevant, but the quantitative conclusions rest on a soft-wall holographic model. Interesting for qualitative mechanisms, weaker as direct phenomenology without stronger model/systematic comparisons.
